description: A left femur with diaphysis and neck. The full description from Leakey and Walker (1985) reads, "This specimen is from the Lower Member below the KBS Tuff in Area 100. It is most of the shaft and neck of a left femur with partof the cancellous bone of the head and distal epiphysis. A length estimate is between 380 and 400. The lesser and greater trochanters have been eroded away. Only part of the area of insertion of the obturators remains. The head is badly worn, exposing the cancellous bone. The epiphyseal line is distinguishable as a plate of more compact bone running through the cancellous tissue of the head. The neck is very long and extremely compressed anteroposteriorly. The estimated length from the intertrochanteric crest to the beginning of the cancellous bone of the head is 45.0. The neck diameters at the middle of the neck are 16.5 anteroposteriorly and 30.0 superoinferiorly. In section the neck at its middle is an elongate ellipse with the long axis directed slightly downwards and backwards from the coronal plane. The shaft is relatively platymeric. The diameters are as follows: just below the lesser trochanter, 18.5 (anteroposteriorly) and 30.5 (mediolaterally); at midshaft, 20.0 (anteroposteriorly) and 24.6 (mediolaterally); and at a point just above the patellar surface, 24.2 (anteroposteriorly) and 33.0 (mediolaterally). The linea aspera is indistinct, perhaps due to surface weathering. The gluteal tuberosity region is marked by an elongate oval hollow in a swelling on the posterolateral part of the shaft, whose center is about 90.0 below the lowest point of the superior margin of the neck. Nearly opposite the gluteal swelling is a low roughened area that disturbs the profile of the medial border of the shaft just below the lesser trochanter. At about midshaft, a break shows the cortex to be thick. It is 9.0 medially, 7.0 laterally, 5.2 anteriorly, and 6.4 posteriorly. The medullary canal has an average diameter of about 8 at the break." (p. 144)
